# DecryptionFailureUsedAsPlaintext

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Security](/rules/#security)

Decryption can fail and return false. Check success before treating the result as plaintext.

## Example

```php{2}
<?php
$plain=openssl_decrypt($cipher,"aes-256-gcm",$key,OPENSSL_RAW_DATA,$iv,$tag); file_put_contents($path,$plain);
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Check decryption success before using the plaintext.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- D1. Resolved openssl_decrypt result is passed to a known string sink file_put_contents data argument or strlen without a false-result guard. Track direct nesting or unmodified locals; arbitrary named consumers are excluded.
- D2. Resolve builtin functions, classes, constants and methods; user-defined lookalikes are excluded. Follow only bounded local proof in one lexical scope.
- D3. A false-result guard is a condition on the same local, still holding the same decryption call, whose outcome on the path to the sink rules out false. Accepted tests, also negated with `!`, parenthesised, or combined (any operand of a true `&&`/`and`, any operand of a false `||`/`or`): strict or loose comparison with `false` on either side, plain truthiness, `empty()`, a resolved builtin `is_string()`, and the assignment of the call written inside the condition. Accepted positions: the matching branch of an enclosing `if`/`elseif`/`else` (later arms count every earlier condition as failed), the matching arm of a ternary, the right operand of a short-circuit operator, and code following an earlier `if` without alternatives whose body always exits, in the same or an enclosing statement list.
- D4. Emit one finding per violating operation, not per supporting evidence statement. Use existing analysis budgets; exhausted proof produces no report.

## Exceptions (no report)

- E1. Do not report unresolved or shadowed builtin names, unknown values, or incomplete receiver/type provenance. Unknown calls, aliases escaping, and intervening writes invalidate local proof. Similar code outside the stated detection contract is not a finding.
- E2. A test of another variable, of an earlier or later value of the local, a `null` comparison, `isset()`, or a guard whose failing branch falls through to the sink is not a guard; the sink is still reported.
- E3. Both standard suppression forms suppress this native ID.
- E4. A value the shared flow analysis proves is not the failure value at the use is never reported, whatever form the proof takes: a test in an enclosing branch, loop condition or short-circuit operand, an early exit, a statement that leaves on the failing outcome (`$v !== false or exit;`, `$v or throw …;`, `$v ?: throw …;`), a failing branch that ends in a call that never returns (a callee declared `never`, or a function or a final or private method every path of which throws or exits), a test stored in a boolean and tested later while neither the boolean nor the tested variable has been written, and, on PHP 8.0 and later outside any `try` with a `catch`, a builtin call that returned after receiving the value for a parameter that only accepts arrays, objects or callables: such a call throws a `TypeError` for `false`. A `switch (true)` case is read like the condition of an `if`/`elseif` chain. Positions PHP may skip prove nothing: the right side of `??=`, the arguments of a null-safe call and anything chained after `?->`. A null-safe call to a never-returning method does not end the path, and `f(...)` creates a closure without calling `f`.

## Fix

None. Choosing a repair requires intent or additional runtime information.

## PHP versions

Available throughout supported PHP 5.3–8.5 where the referenced builtin/extension is available. Respect syntax/version-specific receiver contracts; unavailable APIs are not this rule’s concern.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "DecryptionFailureUsedAsPlaintext": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore DecryptionFailureUsedAsPlaintext
```
